observations: Photo 0 shows a white console with a large circular black mesh vent and a black wireless controller. The word 'XBOX' is visible on the top right.
Photo 1 shows the front edge of the console with a disc slot, confirming it is a model with an optical drive.
Photo 2 shows the side ventilation pattern and a small Xbox logo.
The console has some surface scuffs and marks on the white casing.
A watermark 'WILLIAMS GADGETS' is visible on photos 1 and 2.

claims.evidence: The form factor, white color, circular vent, and disc slot in photos 0 and 1 are characteristic of the Xbox One S.
There is no photo of the system settings screen showing storage capacity.
A black Xbox wireless controller is shown in photos 0 and 1.
There is no photo of the console's digital library or home screen.

risks.risk: The console may not power on or output video.
risks.proof: A video of the console booting to the home screen and navigating menus.

risks.risk: The internal storage may be 500GB instead of the claimed 1TB.
risks.proof: A photo of the 'Settings > System > Storage' screen.

risks.risk: The optical disc drive may be faulty and unable to read games.
risks.proof: A video showing a disc being inserted and the game successfully launching.
risks.if_unproven: as having a broken disc drive

risks.risk: The controller may have stick drift or unresponsive buttons.
risks.proof: A video of the controller being used in a controller test application.

risks.risk: The console could be banned from Xbox Network (Live).
risks.proof: A photo of the network settings showing 'All services are available'.

proof_requests: Video of the console powering on and loading the home screen.
Photo of the storage settings showing the total capacity.
Video of a game disc being inserted and played.
Photo of the network settings screen.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as an Xbox One S. While several functional claims are unverified, it can be priced at its worst-case state (non-functional/500GB/banned) until proof is provided.
